audit_findings.title: FY2026 owner earnings mix partial-year acquired earnings with partial-year financing costs
audit_findings.magnitude: MARS contributed $60.1 million of revenue and $3.9 million of pre-tax income for only five months; filed pro forma FY2026 net income attributable to CSW was $124.394 million versus reported $112.045 million, a $12.349 million difference; OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The $169.3 million OE anchor contains only post-November 4 MARS operations and acquisition interest, while every forecast year represents the combined business for a full year.
audit_findings.evidence: MARS Parts activity has been included in our consolidated results of operations and in the operating results of our Contractor Solutions segment since the November 4, 2025 date of acquisition.
audit_findings.explanation: The timing mismatch is demonstrated, but its direction is unresolved because both acquired operating cash flow and financing costs are incomplete. MARS's $658.1 million purchase price and the filed pro forma earnings difference show that the omitted periods are reasonably capable of materially changing the anchor and scenario values.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild OE using full-year MARS operating results, maintenance reinvestment and working capital together with full-year acquisition interest; then rerun all scenarios with the same share count and bridge rules.

audit_findings.title: Forecast growth may rely on acquisitions whose purchase cost is absent from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Almost $1.2 billion of acquisition investment over fiscal 2024-2026; FY2026 acquired revenue contributed $222.6 million while total revenue increased $204.2 million and organic revenue declined $18.4 million, or 2.1%
audit_findings.mechanism: The 6% base and 9% bull growth rates compound OE without charging the acquisition capital needed if that growth is expected to resemble acquisition-led historical growth.
audit_findings.evidence: We invested almost $1.2 billion in the multiple acquisitions made in fiscal years 2026, 2025 and 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: Recent acquisition dependence is demonstrated, although the record does not establish how the forecast rates were selected. Because acquired revenue exceeded the entire FY2026 revenue increase and the associated investment is large relative to the $2.854 billion base equity value, treating acquisition-led growth as free organic growth could materially overstate value.
audit_findings.action: Decompose historical OE growth into organic and acquired contributions; rerun using supportable organic growth or explicitly subtract the acquisition investment required to reproduce each scenario's acquired growth.

audit_findings.title: Redeemable noncontrolling interest may be an unbridged claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $19.010 million at June 30, 2026, equal to $1.15 per diluted share and 0.67% of the $2.854 billion base equity value; FY2026 income attributable to the interest was $0.802 million and June-quarter income was $0.021 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Value could be overstated if consolidated D&A, working capital or capital expenditures attributable to Shell remain in OE while only Shell's net income is excluded, or if a redemption payment is omitted from the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The Whitmore JV's LLC Agreement contains a put option that gives either member the right to sell its 50 % equity interest in the Whitmore JV to the other member at a dollar amount equivalent to 90 % of the initiating member's equity interest determined based on the fair market value of the Whitmore JV's net assets.
audit_findings.explanation: The allocation issue and bridge treatment remain unresolved, but the filed claim and earnings are small. Even deducting the entire $19.010 million without credit for the additional JV interest acquired would reduce base value by only $1.15 per share and would not alter the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace each Whitmore JV component in the OE reconciliation to CSW's 50% economic interest and document the put treatment; correct the bridge if necessary, without treating the full $19.010 million as debt unless the associated acquired cash flows are also modeled.

audit_findings.title: Remaining contingent acquisition consideration is omitted from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $16.655 million at June 30, 2026, equal to $1.01 per diluted share and 0.58% of the $2.854 billion base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Financing-classified settlement payments can bypass OE, so an unpaid acquisition claim should reduce the equity bridge unless its payments are already charged in projected OE.
audit_findings.evidence: As of March 31, 2026 and 2025, the contingent consideration liability reported in the balance sheets was $ 16.7 million and $ 24.4 million, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The outstanding liability and its omission are demonstrated. Nevertheless, deducting its entire filed fair value would reduce base value by only about $1.01 per share and would not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm that projected OE excludes settlement payments, then deduct the latest $16.655 million fair-value liability from the bridge and update it for later remeasurements or payments.

audit_findings.title: A real Greco perimeter change conflicts with the null perimeter ruling
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2026 Greco US and Canada revenue totaled $33.4 million with combined pre-tax losses of $2.3 million excluding impairment and exit costs; June-quarter revenue totaled $5.5 million with combined pre-tax losses of $1.1 million; June 30 held-for-sale net assets were $6.117 million and remaining Canada exit costs were $1.0-$1.5 million
audit_findings.mechanism: The anchor includes Greco operations and exit effects, while future OE will exclude disposed or exited operations and the bridge should include net proceeds and remaining cash exit costs.
audit_findings.evidence: During the quarter ended March 31, 2026, the Company committed to a plan to pursue a sale of the Greco US business, which is available for immediate sale in its present condition, and the Company has initiated an active program to locate a buyer.
audit_findings.explanation: The null perimeter is demonstrably incorrect, but the filed scale is small: FY2026 Greco revenue was about 3.1% of consolidated revenue, and the businesses generated losses rather than material positive earnings. Removing the losses may raise ongoing OE, while exit costs reduce value and sale proceeds increase it. These amounts are not large enough to alter the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Rerun the anchor and forecast excluding Greco US and Canada operating cash flows, reverse only genuine noncash or nonrecurring exit items, add realizable net sale proceeds, and deduct the filed $1.0-$1.5 million remaining exit-cost estimate.

audit_findings.title: A nonrecurring tax-reserve release may inflate the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $5.2 million, equal to 3.1% of the $169.3 million anchor; if fully included, proportional reruns reduce operating PV by approximately $61.9 million bear, $86.2 million base and $101.6 million bull, or $3.74, $5.22 and $6.15 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: A statute-driven tax benefit included in net income would increase the OE anchor and be capitalized through every forecast year and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: This was partially offset by UTP which decreased the provision by $5.2 million ($6.4 million UTP release offset by $1.0 million of additional penalties and interest) and the effective tax rate by 3.6%.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the OE reconciliation already normalized the benefit is unresolved. Even under the conservative assumption that the entire $5.2 million remains in OE, the computed effect is only about 3.1% of operating value and does not change the conclusion relative to the $308.46 market price.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the FY2026 OE reconciliation; if present, remove the $5.2 million net UTP benefit from the anchor and rerun all three scenarios and the buy-below price.
